original_question: Which chromosome contains the gene encoding the peptide hormone that is typically elevated in parathyroid carcinoma?

final_qi.question: Which chromosome contains the gene encoding the peptide hormone that is typically elevated in parathyroid carcinoma?
final_qi.long_answer: Parathyroid carcinoma characteristically causes markedly elevated levels of parathyroid hormone (PTH). The human PTH gene is located on the short arm of chromosome 11 (band 11p15.3), so chromosome 11 harbors the gene encoding the peptide hormone that rises in this malignancy.
